name: cloud_ops
description: Execute AWS cloud operations via the AWS CLI for infrastructure monitoring, health checks, and supervised remediation. Covers EC2 instance management, RDS database monitoring, ELB/ALB target health, CloudWatch metrics and alarms, and SQS queue depth monitoring. All read-only Describe/Get/List operations are safe for autonomous execution. State-changing operations (start, stop, reboot, terminate) require confirmation via the infrastructure_ops skill guardrails.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: AWS CLI command arguments. Examples: 'ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=app-server', 'rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier my-db', 'elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>', 'cloudwatch describe-alarms --state-value ALARM', 'sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url <url> --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessages'. Do NOT include the 'aws' prefix — it is added automatically.

usage_guidance:
Use for ALL AWS cloud infrastructure operations. Before executing, consult the infrastructure_ops skill for routing and guardrail checks.

**Read-only commands** (autonomous — no confirmation needed):
  ec2 describe-instances, ec2 describe-instance-status, rds describe-db-instances,
  rds describe-db-clusters, elbv2 describe-target-health, elbv2 describe-load-balancers,
  cloudwatch describe-alarms, cloudwatch get-metric-data, cloudwatch list-metrics,
  sqs get-queue-attributes, sqs list-queues, autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups

**Low-risk mutations** (log and confirm via skill):
  ec2 start-instances, ec2 reboot-instances, autoscaling set-desired-capacity

**High-risk mutations** (require human approval):
  ec2 stop-instances, ec2 terminate-instances, rds stop-db-instance,
  rds delete-db-instance, rds reboot-db-instance

**Blocked operations** (never execute — escalate to human):
  iam *, route53 *, organizations *, kms delete-key, s3 rb

Always use --output json for structured output. Use --region to specify the target region explicitly.
returns: Command output from AWS CLI in JSON format (when --output json is used). Error output includes AWS error codes, messages, and request IDs.
